title: The blessings of God on you! Buck Mulligan cried, jumping up from his chair.
html_source:
Throughout this chapter, one may observe Mulligan often using such expressions as, “The blessings of God on you”, or another with “a miracle!” He also displays his fluency in Catholic matters, through such instances as “In nomina Patris et Spiritus Sancti”, or “Lead him not into temptation, which may also lead one to believe that he is aware of the fourth commandment—which states that “thou shalt not take the Lord thy God in vain"—though he proceeds to bestow "the blessings of God” to a woman bringing milk for his beverage.

Mulligan does, however, display a great deal of enthusiasm to the milk’s arrival, “jumping from his chair”, but might easily be perceived as quite the blasphemer by the Holy Roman Catholic and Apostolic Church from the nature of many of his expressions.

He also displays his capacity to societal indifference, with one instance being his noting Stephen’s mother’s death, “ O, it’s only Dedalus whose mother is beastly dead”, and his reaction to Stephen bringing that point up, “A flush which made him seem younger and more engaging rose to Buck Mulligan’s cheek”, from which he proceeds to rebuke Stephen for his prolonged grieving. This indifference is seen elsewhere in Mulligan’s manner.
